### Observed differences

- A03 was not observed in any of the 200 earlier-window traces; in the later window it occurs exactly once in about 52 in 100 traces, with no repeats within a trace. [OCC001]
- When it occurs, A03 sits a bit over a third of the way through the case (median normalised position about 0.38, quartiles about 0.25–0.42); earlier it had no observed positions at all. [POS001]
- New transitions appeared around A03. In the later window its observed outgoing transitions go to A12 (about 36 in 100), A11 (about 35) and A08 (about 29); A08 now sends about 38 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A03 (earlier it split between A11, about 51, and A12, about 49), and A12 now sends about 33 in 100 to A03 (earlier A08 about 51, A11 about 49). [DIR001, DIR003, DIR004]
- A03 now co-occurs with A05, A08, A11 and A12 in about 52 in 100 traces — essentially exactly the traces in which it occurs — whereas earlier these pairs never co-occurred (each of the other activities appeared without A03 in about 51 in 100 traces). A03 always runs before A11; it runs after A05 in about 28 in 100 co-occurring traces (interleaved in about 24); with A08 and A12 both orders occur in similar shares (roughly 23–29 in 100 each). [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004]
- Gaps between previously adjacent activities widened by about one step in a subset of cases: A08→A12 is now 2 steps apart in about 40 in 100 occurrences (earlier always 1) and A12→A08 in about 32; A12→A11 and A08→A11, earlier at 1–2 steps, now reach 3 steps in about 33–38 in 100; A05→A11, earlier most often 3 steps (about 43 in 100) with about 19 in 100 at 5 steps, is now uniformly 4 steps. [LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG002, LAG001]
- The other activities' participation is essentially unchanged (A05 and A11 each appear in about 51 in 100 traces in both windows) and A11's position is stable; A05's typical position moved slightly earlier (mean about 0.18 to about 0.11, median to the first event). [POS002, POS003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that A03 became an active step in the later window, executed once in about half of the cases and inserted into the existing mid-process block: it follows A05's early segment (mostly after A05, sometimes interleaved), is woven between A08 and A12 in both orders, and always completes before A11. The insertion is shown directly by the new edges A08→A03, A12→A03 and A03→{A08, A11, A12}, by A03's participation rising from 0 to about 52 in 100 traces at a stable mid-early position, and by the one-step widening of previously adjacent pairs. All 17 qualifying items are control-flow items from a screening that expected about 0.17 without change across 35 tested units, and every difference exceeds 99.5 in 100 random re-splits, so the pattern as a whole is unlikely under sampling noise; note that the items describe one underlying difference, so they corroborate rather than independently confirm it. Limitations: zero earlier participation shows only that A03 was not observed before, not that it was newly introduced — a previously very rare variant that grew to half of the cases cannot be ruled out — and the evidence cannot show why only about half of the cases contain A03 (an optional step versus a path taken by half of the cases); the collapse of the A05→A11 distance to exactly 4 steps is also only partly explained by a simple one-step insertion. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005]

Other differences: A05's outgoing transitions shifted away from A07 (about 58 in 100 earlier to about 45 in 100 later, with A03 now receiving about 16), and A11's position spread narrowed slightly (standard deviation about 0.12 to 0.08); these fit the reorganisation around A03 but are not needed for the hypothesis. [DIR002, POS003]
